title: Efficient Estimation of Word Representations in Vector Space
summary: Shows that simple shallow networks trained on huge text corpora produce word vectors where directions carry meaning, for example king minus man plus woman lands near queen.
why: This is where embeddings, the basis of semantic search and RAG, became practical.

title: Adam: A Method for Stochastic Optimization
summary: Combines momentum with per-parameter adaptive step sizes so training works well with little tuning.
why: Adam and its variant AdamW are the default optimizers you will see in nearly every training script.

title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition
summary: Adds skip connections so each block learns a correction to its input, which makes very deep networks trainable.
why: Residual connections appear in every transformer block, so this idea is inside every LLM.

title: Attention Is All You Need
summary: Replaces recurrence with self-attention, letting every token look at every other token in parallel, and introduces the transformer architecture.
why: Every modern LLM is a variation of this design. Read it right after building a small GPT.

title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers
summary: Pretrains a bidirectional transformer by masking words and predicting them, then fine-tunes it on downstream tasks.
why: Introduced the pretrain-then-fine-tune recipe and the encoder models that still power embeddings and rerankers.

title: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models
summary: Finds that language model loss falls as a smooth power law with more parameters, data, and compute.
why: Explains why labs keep scaling and helps you reason about model size, cost, and quality tradeoffs.

title: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners
summary: Shows a 175B-parameter model can perform new tasks from a few examples in the prompt, with no weight updates.
why: The origin of prompting as an engineering discipline and of in-context learning.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
summary: Combines a retriever over a document index with a generator so answers are conditioned on retrieved passages.
why: The original RAG design. Your RAG chatbot project is a modern version of it.

title: An Image is Worth 16x16 Words: Transformers for Image Recognition at Scale
summary: Splits an image into patches, treats them as tokens, and feeds them to a standard transformer.
why: Shows transformers work beyond text, which is the basis of most multimodal models.

title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
summary: Freezes the base model and trains small low-rank matrices added to its layers, cutting trainable parameters by orders of magnitude.
why: The standard way to fine-tune on modest hardware. You will use it in your fine-tuning project.

title: Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models
summary: Prompting a model to write out intermediate steps substantially improves accuracy on arithmetic and reasoning problems.
why: The idea behind reasoning prompts and the reasoning models that followed.

title: Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models
summary: Finds that for a fixed compute budget, models and training data should grow together, and many earlier models were undertrained.
why: Changed how models are sized and why smaller models trained longer can beat bigger ones.

title: Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback
summary: Fine-tunes a model with supervised examples and reinforcement learning from human preferences so it follows instructions better.
why: The recipe that turned base models into assistants like ChatGPT.

title: FlashAttention: Fast and Memory-Efficient Exact Attention
summary: Reorganizes the attention computation to reduce reads and writes to slow GPU memory, giving exact attention that is much faster.
why: Explains why long contexts became affordable and why serving stacks depend on optimized kernels.

title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
summary: Has the model alternate between writing a reasoning step and taking a tool action, feeding each observation back into the next step.
why: The pattern behind most tool-using agents.

title: Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback
summary: Trains a model to critique and revise its own outputs against a written set of principles, using AI feedback instead of only human labels.
why: A practical view of alignment and of how principles can steer model behavior.

title: Toolformer: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Use Tools
summary: A model learns when and how to call external tools such as a calculator or search by training on its own useful API calls.
why: Background for function calling and why tool use is a learnable skill.

title: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
summary: An agent writes short reflections on its failures and stores them in memory so later attempts improve without weight updates.
why: A simple, useful pattern for agents that learn from feedback inside a loop.

title: QLoRA: Efficient Finetuning of Quantized LLMs
summary: Fine-tunes LoRA adapters on top of a 4-bit quantized base model, making large-model fine-tuning possible on a single GPU.
why: The reason you can fine-tune sizable open models on affordable hardware.

title: Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model
summary: Optimizes a model directly on pairs of preferred and rejected answers with a simple loss, skipping a separate reward model and RL loop.
why: A simpler and widely used alternative to RLHF for preference tuning.

title: Tree of Thoughts: Deliberate Problem Solving with Large Language Models
summary: Lets a model explore several reasoning branches, evaluate them, and backtrack instead of following a single chain.
why: Shows how search and self-evaluation can improve hard reasoning tasks.

title: Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena
summary: Studies using a strong model to grade other models' answers and reports where the judge agrees with humans and where it is biased.
why: Essential for building evals: it explains both the promise and the biases of LLM-as-judge.

title: Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts
summary: Finds that models use information at the start and end of a long prompt better than information in the middle.
why: Directly affects how you order and trim retrieved passages in RAG.

title: Llama 2: Open Foundation and Fine-Tuned Chat Models
summary: Describes how an open-weights family of chat models was pretrained, fine-tuned, and safety-tuned.
why: A readable end-to-end account of how a modern assistant model is built.

title: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection
summary: Trains a model to decide when to retrieve, and to critique both the retrieved passages and its own answer.
why: Points toward adaptive RAG, where retrieval is a decision and not a fixed step.

title: Mamba: Linear-Time Sequence Modeling with Selective State Spaces
summary: A sequence model based on selective state spaces that scales linearly with length and competes with transformers on language.
why: The best-known alternative to attention, useful for understanding where architectures may go.

title: DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning
summary: Shows that reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards can produce strong step-by-step reasoning, and describes distilling it into smaller models.
why: A clear public account of how reasoning models are trained.
